TECHNOLOGY.EFFECTIVE_SPECIFICATION: Proposed Technology revision for the human-approved requirements revision ISSUE36-REALTIME-REPLACEMENT. The proposal selects ntfy and UnifiedPush as the sole realtime transport. No human approval of this Technology revision has been recorded. Implementation and downstream GRACE stages remain gated.

VERSION_BASELINE.COMPONENT: Retain the repository's current Go minimum; this technology revision does not upgrade the toolchain.
Use the standard library HTTP client for outbound Web Push requests and existing HTTP primitives; do not add an ntfy-specific client library.
Retain the existing PostgreSQL driver and transaction support.
Retain the existing migration dependency; this revision does not authorize or define database migrations.
Retain the existing project-approved PostgreSQL 18.4 baseline. This revision does not change the database server version.
Reuse the existing session-bound DPoP contract without changing its API or introducing a new authentication scheme.

Use a self-hosted ntfy server as the only realtime push server. The official release notes identify v2.34.0, released 2026-10-24, as current stable. This is a target version decision, not authorization to deploy or change infrastructure.
The ntfy Android application is the initial UnifiedPush distributor target. BFE Chat, not the ntfy application UI, creates the user-visible chat notification.

Official Android connector for registration and delivery of UnifiedPush messages. This client dependency belongs to the Android client repository and is recorded here only as an interoperability target; no other repository is changed by this task.

Use the standardized Android connector/distributor contract. The backend receives the registration endpoint and encryption keys through the authenticated Chat API; route shapes remain for downstream contracts.

ISSUE36_TECHNOLOGY_REVISION.SCOPE: Proposed Technology revision for the human-approved ISSUE36-REALTIME-REPLACEMENT requirements. It replaces Centrifuge with ntfy and UnifiedPush as the sole realtime push path. It does not authorize implementation, dependency edits, client changes, tests, deployment, infrastructure changes, or downstream GRACE artifacts. Human approval of this exact Technology revision is still required.
ISSUE36_TECHNOLOGY_REVISION.DECISION: Use a self-hosted ntfy server v2.34.0 as the only realtime push server and the ntfy Android application v1.25.2 as the initial UnifiedPush distributor. The Android BFE Chat application integrates the official UnifiedPush connector, receives the push in its own process, and creates the Android system notification itself. ntfy is not used as a second notification UI. Remove Centrifuge from the active target; do not retain WebSocket/Centrifuge delivery, a fallback transport, a parallel transport, or a compatibility path.

Use the UnifiedPush registration endpoint and its p256dh public key and auth secret as the Web Push subscription. Encrypt payloads according to RFC 8291 using the required aes128gcm content encoding. The Go 1.27.3 standard library provides the required cryptographic primitives, including P-256 ECDH, HKDF-SHA256, and AES-GCM; use these primitives rather than adding an external dependency solely for these primitives. The implementation must follow the RFC encoding precisely and pass interoperability verification against the selected ntfy version.

The decrypted application payload contains exactly the protocol version and opaque wakeToken. It must not contain message text, conversation/account identifiers, document ID/title/content, sender identity, or any other identifying metadata. Do not use ntfy title/body/click URL fields to expose conversation details. BFE Chat displays a generic system notification and keeps the wakeToken only in the notification's internal navigation state.

Generate wakeToken using a cryptographically secure random source and maintain a durable server-side mapping from each issued token to its conversation. Do not assign a fixed TTL or delete mappings by age while an issued notification may still be delivered, queued, retried, or activated. Resolution is repeatable and does not consume or invalidate the token; token reuse is allowed but reuse of one token across all notifications for a conversation is not mandated. The token is a reference only, never a credential or authorization grant. Every resolution revalidates the DPoP-bound session, current Chat availability, membership, and message visibility before returning conversation information.

Store each UnifiedPush registration endpoint, public encryption key, and authentication secret as protected subscription data associated with the authenticated BFE account that registered it. Registration, replacement, and removal use the authenticated Chat API and existing DPoP-bound session; concrete routes and request/response schemas belong to downstream GRACE contracts. A subscription identifies a delivery destination only and grants no access to conversations or history. Never return another account’s registration data or write endpoint URLs, authentication secrets, wakeToken values, or full push payloads to logs.

Treat the registered push endpoint as a bearer capability. Require HTTPS and require its origin to match the configured ntfy server origin. Reject arbitrary client-supplied hosts, redirects, invalid schemes, and origins outside the configured ntfy server to prevent server-side request forgery. The endpoint value cannot expand the configured destination origin.

Run ntfy v2.34.0 as a private self-hosted HTTPS instance with auth-default-access: deny-all. Follow the documented ntfy UnifiedPush distributor setup: the BFE Chat publisher uses anonymous write-only access to the up* topic pattern and has no ntfy account/admin credentials; the ntfy Android distributor uses a regular non-admin account with read-only access to the up* topic pattern. Never grant anonymous read or read-write access, and never grant anonymous access to all topics. Use the endpoint and topic returned by the ntfy UnifiedPush registration. Encrypt each payload according to RFC 8291 for its registered endpoint; ntfy topic access does not replace Chat API authorization. Do not expose ntfy administrative credentials to BFE Chat or end-user clients.

On receipt, BFE Chat creates a generic Android system notification with an internal intent containing only wakeToken and protocol version. Tapping it calls the protected Chat API to resolve wakeToken; only a successful current authorization check permits navigation to the conversation and authenticated history retrieval. Invalid, stale, revoked, or disabled-state tokens fail closed without revealing conversation identity or message content.

When Chat is administratively disabled, deny new Chat operations, history requests, wakeToken resolution, and new UnifiedPush registrations. An already-active ntfy subscription may continue delivering only the opaque wake payload; receiving it does not authorize any API request. After re-enable, authorized clients catch up through the existing history API. Do not introduce session revocation, periodic Drive-session checks, or a fixed delivery-stop deadline.

Commit the message before attempting ntfy delivery. A delivery failure never rolls back a persisted message; record the failure without logging secrets. An idempotent message replay must not create a new logical notification. Missed messages are recovered through authenticated history. The specific retry or queue mechanism is not fixed by this technology decision and must preserve these behaviors.

Retain PostgreSQL 18.4, pgx, Goose, native net/http, and the existing BFE Drive Internal Auth UDS/DPoP contract. Realtime events are hints only; persisted conversation history remains authoritative for catch-up, ordering, visibility, and read state. No API versioning, data migration, or legacy-client support is introduced by this technology choice.
ISSUE36_TECHNOLOGY_REVISION.OPEN_QUESTION: Runtime interoperability among ntfy server v2.34.0, ntfy Android distributor v1.25.2, and Android UnifiedPush connector 3.3.5 has not been tested in this Technology-only change. Independent verification must confirm RFC 8291 aes128gcm delivery using the selected Go standard-library primitives, documented anonymous write-only publishing and authenticated distributor read-only access to up*, configured-origin endpoint validation, offline delivery, notification activation, and fail-closed token resolution before implementation can be accepted. This is a verification gate, not approval to change another GRACE artifact now.
ISSUE36_TECHNOLOGY_REVISION.GATE: Technology revision is proposed and awaits explicit Human Approval. The existing ISSUE32 approvals remain historical provenance only. No implementation, test changes, dependency changes, deployment, infrastructure mutation, or downstream GRACE stage is authorized until the relevant approval gate is satisfied.
